chunks.arabic_text: أَلْكِفَايَةُ: عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، وَعَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى، عَنْ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ سَيْفِ بْنِ عُمَيْرَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: From Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, and from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: عَالِمٌ يَنْتَفِعُ بِعِلْمِهِ أَفْضَلُ مِنْ سَبْعِينَ أَلْفَ عَابِدٍ

translations.en: The scholar whose knowledge benefits others is better than seventy thousand worshippers.

en.summary: This hadith emphasizes the superior merit of a scholar whose knowledge is actively utilized to benefit others, ranking him higher than seventy thousand worshippers. It highlights the value of practical knowledge and teaching in Islamic spirituality.
en.seo_question: What is the spiritual merit of a scholar who benefits others compared to worshippers?
